build/guard-standalone.js.3: * Standalone guard: **no third-party emulator file** may appear in an installer.
build/guard-standalone.js.5: * Why a build-time check is necessary:
build/guard-standalone.js.6: *   ApkStart installers (NSIS / portable / MSIX) must work out of the box -- they carry emulator +
build/guard-standalone.js.7: *   platform-tools + the system image, so the app runs right after install without asking users to install MuMu / LDPlayer / BlueStacks.
build/guard-standalone.js.8: *   Since 0.5.6 it goes further: **the code has no third-party backend at all** -- it is not "bundled runtime + optional
build/guard-standalone.js.9: *   reuse" but "bundled runtime only". So besides binaries, this also blocks the backend adapter sources
build/guard-standalone.js.10: *   (backends/mumu.js / backends/fydeos.js / mumu-compat.js) -- if anyone adds them back, the build fails
build/guard-standalone.js.11: *   outright, so a path that takes over someone else's emulator cannot quietly return.
build/guard-standalone.js.13: *   This constraint is easy to break silently: someone copies a MuMu directory into build/runtime as the runtime,
build/guard-standalone.js.14: *   or drops an emulator directory into resources before packaging. The app still works on the dev machine,
build/guard-standalone.js.15: *   but users end up having to install another emulator -- a problem that only shows up on someone else's PC.
build/guard-standalone.js.16: *   Hence a filename scan before packaging that fails the build on any hit.
build/guard-standalone.js.23: * Once these names appear in build output, someone's emulator has been bundled.
build/guard-standalone.js.24: * Match only each emulator's own signature filenames, never broad patterns like /android/, to avoid false positives.
